payload.title: GPU Memory Hierarchy and Optimization
payload.summary: The core of GPU performance optimization is understanding the memory hierarchy and properly leveraging the bandwidth and latency characteristics of each storage level.

sections.heading: Memory Types Overview
sections.gist: table columns: Memory Type, Location, Scope, Lifetime, Latency, Bandwidth, Typical Size

sections.heading: Register Optimization
sections.gist: Registers are the fastest storage, but their quantity is limited (typically 64K 32-bit registers per SM).

sections.heading: Global Memory Optimization
sections.gist: Global memory is the largest but slowest storage.

sections.heading: Shared Memory Optimization
sections.gist: Shared memory is on-chip programmable cache with bandwidth far exceeding that of global memory.

sections.heading: Local Memory
sections.gist: The name is misleading—local memory actually resides in **off-chip device memory**, with latency and bandwidth identical to global memory.

sections.heading: Constant Memory
sections.gist: - Total 64 KB, globally read-only - Ideal for scenarios where all threads read the same value (broadcast within a warp, a single read suffices) - When threads within a warp read different addresses, accesses are serialized; in such cases, …

sections.heading: Host-Device Data Transfer Optimization
sections.gist: PCIe bandwidth (~16 GB/s) is far lower than device memory bandwidth (hundreds of GB/s to several TB/s).
